title: Modern Programming Fundamentals
description: Introduces students to the foundational principles of programming through algorithmic problem solving and Python programming, including values, variables, data types, expressions, conditionals, loops, functions, standard libraries, and an introduction to object-oriented programming.

title: Data Structures
description: Introduces data structures and their use in efficient software development, including structured data abstraction, arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, deques, balanced search trees, heaps, hash tables, and related algorithms and applications.
prerequisites: CSCI 141 or DATA 141 or CSCI 140 or DATA 140

title: Logic and Discrete Structures
description: Covers theoretical foundations of computer science, including propositional and predicate logic, sets, functions, Boolean algebra, proof techniques, counting, discrete probability, relations, trees, and graphs.
prerequisites: CSCI 141 or CSCI 142 or CSCI 140 or DATA 140 or DATA 141

title: Software Development
description: An introduction to principled software development, emphasizing design at the module level as well as tools and techniques. Topics include object-oriented class design and implementation, abstraction techniques, debugging techniques, defensive programming, development and analysis tools, and testing. Emphasizes the role of the individual programmer in large software development projects.

title: Algorithms
description: A systematic study of algorithms and their complexity, including searching, sorting, selecting, graph algorithms, algorithm design methods such as greedy algorithms, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, and backtracking, and an introduction to NP-complete problems.

title: Computer Organization
description: Organization of computer hardware and software; virtual machines, computer systems organization, machine language, assembler language and microprogramming.

title: Principles of Programming Languages
description: A study of programming language principles and paradigms. Formal syntax, including grammars, and semantics. Paradigms, including: imperative, object oriented, functional, logic, event-driven, and concurrent. Run-time implementation issues, including: memory management, parameter passing, and event handling.

title: Large Language Models
description: This course dives into the realm of large language models (LLMs), the engines driving today's natural language processing revolution. Students will master the theory, architecture, and real-world applications of LLMs, preparing to harness our future AI applications. Blending lectures, hands-on coding, and critical analysis, this course equips students with the skills to build, apply, and interrogate these linguistic models.

title: Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning
description: This course will give an overview of important concepts, techniques, and algorithms in artificial intelligence with emphasis on machine learning, beginning with topics such as linear regression and ending up with more recent topics such as boosting, support vector machines, and expectation maximization. The course will give the student the basic ideas and intuition behind modern methods as well as a bit more formal understanding of how, why, and when they work.

title: Database Systems
description: Design, organization and implementation of database management systems: file organization and processing, hierarchical, network, and relational models of database structure, data definition and data manipulation languages, security and integrity of databases, and the study of existing database implementations.

title: Finite Automata and Theory of Computation
description: Theory of sequential machines, finite automata, Turing machines, recursive functions, computability of functions.

title: Data Mining
description: Introduction to fundamental concepts and techniques in data mining, specifically, basic data mining concepts, graph mining, traditional clustering and classification methods, as well as recent deep learning techniques.

title: Principles of Operating Systems
description: The conceptual view of an operating system as a collection of concurrent processes; semaphores, monitors and rendezvous. Real and virtual memory organization and management, processor allocation and management, and external device management.

title: Neural Networks for Machine Learning
description: Machine learning enables computers to learn from experience. The first part of the course will cover foundational topics in pattern recognition and machine learning such as probability distributions, linear models for regression, and linear models for classification. The second part of the course will examine nonlinear models for regression and classification, focusing on artificial neural networks. Neural networks are being used to achieve state-of-the-art performance at applications in different modalities and domains. Students will be required to analyze and present relevant research papers.

title: Computer and Network Security
description: An introduction to the principles and practices of cryptography, network security, and secure software. Cryptography topics includes: basic methods, key distribution, and protocols for authenticated and confidential communications. The practice of network security includes: Kerberos, PGP, public key infrastructures, SSL/TLS. IP security, intrusion detection, password management, firewalls, viruses and worms, and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development
description: GenAI for Software Development provides students with a strong foundation in the principles and technical expertise needed to develop and apply Deep Learning (DL)-based systems, with a particular emphasis on Generative AI methods. The course focuses on leveraging advanced techniques to enhance software development processes, addressing practices such as source code generation, automated documentation, and other key aspects of modern software engineering. By the end of the course, students will possess a comprehensive understanding of Generative AI methods for software development. This includes the ability to design and implement new DL-based approaches to address challenges in the software engineering domain, critically analyze the latest advancements in the field, and propose innovative solutions to refine Generative AI techniques.

title: Penetration Testing
description: This course introduces computer network vulnerability assessments and penetration testing. The course explores how malicious actors and hackers attack computers and networks and how to protect against these threats. This is a hands-on learning course where students will be exposed to and perform various types of vulnerability assessments and explore penetration testing techniques in order to understand how to defend against cyber-attacks. Legal implications and ethical issues will also be addressed.

title: Applied Topology Data Science
description: This course introduces applied topology—new algorithms for probing the shape and structure of complex data arising in computing, data science, and physics. We begin with foundational concepts of topology such as topological spaces, continuous maps, and connectedness. Then we examine tools of topological data analysis, including simplicial complexes, persistent homology, persistence diagrams, and stability. The course emphasizes the idea that data are not only points to be fit or classified but also objects with multiscale structure that can reveal loops, voids, and connectivity patterns. These patterns elude traditional machine learning approaches, particularly in noisy, high-dimensional settings. Students will work with real datasets, compute topological invariants, and use these features in artificial intelligence and machine learning models, while also learning where topological methods succeed and where they break down.

title: Reasoning with Generative AI
description: Reasoning with Generative AI examines how modern generative systems can be used to support disciplined reasoning grounded in evidence. Students learn to move from raw inputs to reasoned outputs by combining traditional analytic thinking with contemporary generative AI tools, while learning how data is represented, how generative models process data, and how to use these tools responsibly.
prerequisites: CSCI 140 or CSCI 141 or DATA 141 or AAI 101

title: Data in the Age of AI
description: Prepares students to design credible analyses in a world where information is often incomplete, algorithmically mediated, or partially generated. Students learn about major AI approaches, evaluate their appropriate uses, judge quality, and recognize when generative tools can extend an analysis or introduce risks and distortions.
prerequisites: CSCI 140 or CSCI 141 or DATA 141 or DATA 101 or AAI 101

title: AI & Data Ethics
description: Introduces critical, ethical, and moral issues surrounding data, AI, and society. The course blends social and historical perspectives on data and algorithmic systems with ethics, policy, and case examples and examines privacy, surveillance, discrimination, transparency, responsibility, and trust across the data and AI lifecycle.

title: Applied Linear Algebra & Calculus
description: Introduces core mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence and computing, including linear algebra, matrix decompositions, calculus, and differential equations with direct application to machine learning, optimization, and simulation.

title: Research Design and Statistics
description: Introduces principles of empirical inquiry, statistical modeling, and computational experimentation in data-rich and AI-supported environments, including research design, simulation-based inference, likelihood-based estimation, confidence intervals, model comparison, Bayesian updating, and reproducible workflows.

title: Applied Machine Learning
description: Focuses on the technical application of machine learning algorithms, their nature, and the potential drawbacks and advantages of different classes of algorithms. Topics include probability, distributions, Monte-Carlo simulations, reinforcement learning, association rules, nonlinear regression, support vector machines, model selection, diagnostics, neural networks and deep learning, natural language processing, and related approaches.

title: Databases
description: Students learn relational database design and SQL programming using Python and SQLite, creating relational databases from real and synthetic data and querying and updating data with an emphasis on validation techniques.

title: Data Visualization
description: Provides an overview of data visualization theory and develops the ability to select effective visualization approaches, identify outcomes for data challenges, and create visualizations using industry-standard software and artificial intelligence tools.

title: Special Topics in Data Application
description: Selected topics in Data Science that count toward the Data Applications track. The topic is announced before the semester; the course may be repeated only when covering a separate topic.
prerequisites: To be determined by topic each term

title: Trustworthy AI
description: Explores ethical, legal, and technical dimensions of building trustworthy artificial intelligence systems, including fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, robustness, privacy-preserving machine learning, and algorithmic bias.

title: Agentic Coordination
description: Examines the design, implementation, and deployment of teams of AI agents powered by large language models and related technologies. Topics include advanced prompt engineering, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, agent architectures, memory systems, evaluation, safety, and human-in-the-loop design.

title: Spatial Data Discovery
description: A capstone course focused on spatial data discovery using Python programming, large data repositories, data harmonization, processing, modeling, visualization, and open-source GIS software.

title: Special Topics
description: Selected topics in Data Science. The course is designed to meet the capstone requirement; topics are announced before the semester and instructors may require prior approval. Students complete a project to fulfill the capstone requirement.

title: Advanced Applications of AI
description: Focuses on data discovery and analysis using disparate open-access data sources and advanced analytical and machine learning methods including variable selection, nonparametric regression, functional data analysis, and deep learning. Students communicate findings through an HTML data science paper.

title: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
description: Teaches the foundations of neural networks and deep learning, including data preprocessing, neural network building blocks, RNNs, convolutional networks, computer vision, backpropagation, transfer approaches, and technical implementations using common machine learning frameworks.

title: Agent-Based Modeling
description: Uses openly accessible satellite, household survey, and other data with machine learning and spatial statistics to construct agent-based models of human development processes. Students use Python, Java, and R to build modules and simulations.

title: Network Analysis
description: Surveys fundamental topics in network science, including social networks, hubs, directed and weighted networks, and the spread of information and misinformation in social media.
prerequisites: DATA 301 (may be taken concurrently) or DATA 310

title: Generative AI
description: Explores foundational theories and practical applications of generative AI, including GANs, VAEs, and transformer models, with hands-on training, tuning, and deployment of generative models in Python using machine learning libraries.

title: Bayesian Reasoning in Data Science
description: Introduces conditional probability and Bayesian reasoning in data science, using real-world examples and computational implementations to connect Bayesian concepts with programming.

title: Reinforcement Learning
description: Introduces reinforcement learning fundamentals, including Markov decision processes, planning, function approximation, Q-learning, and policy-gradient methods, with hands-on Python projects.

title: Web Science
description: Provides an overview of the World Wide Web and associated decentralized information structures, focusing on web architecture, web analysis, web archiving, social networks, search engines, web mining, information diffusion, and the Semantic Web.

title: Artificial Intelligence Systems
description: Introduces foundational principles of automation in artificial intelligence and data science, emphasizing repeatable, scalable, production-ready workflows, automated data pipelines, quality assurance, scheduling, monitoring, and AI deployment.

title: Automation & Workflows
description: Focuses on automation and documented workflows for reproducible, efficient, and maintainable data analyses. Students develop program prototypes and documentation for peer testing and critique, culminating in a final project with written documentation and a working demonstration.

title: Independent Research in Data Science
description: Allows students with a focus in Data Science to engage in independent research under the supervision of a program faculty member. Students conduct a substantial research project involving synthesis and critical analysis and communicate their work to diverse audiences. May be repeated for credit.

title: Honors - Data Science
description: Honors thesis research conducted by Data Science majors under the supervision of a faculty member. Students in the DATA 495/DATA 496 sequence write an honors thesis based on a literature review and findings from their research project.

title: Internship
description: Provides first-hand knowledge through practical experience in real-world settings. Students are supervised by and meet regularly with department faculty members during the course. Academic credit requires faculty approval prior to participation.

Introduction to Remotely Sensed Imagery and Analysis
